tagline: Between the ridges and the farms of northwest Georgia.
intro: The byway runs 51 miles through northwest Georgia on US 27, State Routes 156 and 136 and rural county roads, bordered by mountain overlooks and fertile farmland. A steep gravel road leaves it for the deck at John's Mountain Overlook, on a mountain named for John Fields, a Cherokee. Nearby, The Pocket was a Civilian Conservation Corps camp from 1938 until 1942, and some of its remains can still be seen.
The country around holds Cherokee history, Civil War battles and farmhouses from the 1800s that still stand.

moments.title: Subligna
moments.text: The name is a Latin construct meaning "under wood", a compliment to a settler named Dr. William Dunlap Underwood.

moments.title: Villanow
moments.text: Cavender's Country Store, dated to around 1840 though locals dispute the year, once sold the valley anything from buggies to caskets, and it is closed now.

practical: The steep gravel road up to John's Mountain Overlook closes in winter, January through early March.
